verification: JSDOM UI event checks only; native dragging, visual rendering and Windows integration not verified
nativeAcceptance: Versioned owner mouse acceptance is recorded separately in docs/product-v3/drag-feedback-20261019.json; this verifier does not perform native dragging.

checks.name: Highlight preserves exact raw text, empty and duplicate elements, and escapes markup
Whole-string highlights only exact matches; blanks are not matched as list elements
Workbench highlights just the selected Path element, leaving other elements unmarked
Workbench double click opens shared editor with raw values and demo metadata
Edit, move, add and delete stay in draft; cancel restores focus and snapshot
Explicit workbench edit button provides a discoverable alternative
Windows table shows snapshot without scheme highlights and shares the direct editor
Keyboard entry and Escape close editor without changing demo data
Empty segments, repeated values and whitespace survive the editor unchanged
Keyboard ordering retains stable row identity and input focus
Drag/drop event handlers reorder elements without deduplication
Separator validation prevents ambiguous element input while retaining typed text
Apply updates only demo snapshot, keeps raw order, and records a demo history item
Deleting all elements removes the Windows value rather than persisting an empty string
Special value stays whole with semicolons and hides element sorting controls
All schemes copy is simple and group headings separate name, count and flags
Opaque full-row overlay preserves dimensions, live controls and hotspot while native drag bitmap is blank
Drag image cleanup covers replacement, normal/no-op row drops, end drops and dismiss without changing occurrence identity
Vertical rail previews a full slot, moves neighbours and commits only the selected occurrence on drop
Dragging down opens an end slot and cancellation preserves raw order and row identities
Fast cross-list moves ignore stale source samples and keep a stationary landing slot quiet
A small slot boundary dead band prevents rapid reverse shuffling without blocking a deliberate move
Scrolled list bounds and landing slots use the same current viewport coordinates
The empty space opened by neighbours accepts a drop on the list itself
Overlay document/source tracking detaches on external drop, next drag, render, dragend and dismiss
Pointer release outside the list commits the same row, baseline/preview badges and counts as move buttons
Dragging identical occurrences produces movement feedback in both comparison panes even when raw result is unchanged
Pointer cancellation and click-only gestures preserve both comparison panes and release capture
Fast pointer reversals settle on frozen slots without repeated neighbour mutations or stale native samples
Dropping back into the same slot does not redraw the list or pretend a move occurred
A ghost can be pointer-dragged with both comparison markers while its deletion draft stays out of the result
pointer release continues from the visible lifted row instead of replaying its opening position
native release continues from the visible lifted row instead of replaying its opening position
An already settled lift stays at the destination on release without a second movement animation
Ghost release also lands from its current visible position while preserving removal and movement feedback
Shared component and additional stylesheet are local; no UI runtime errors
